description: pulselog-strict-live-3 — authored through the bareloop panel (green, js)

jobLines.text: Run npm run typecheck -- --strict and fix every error it reports in src/checks.js, until that command reports zero errors in src/checks.js.
jobLines.rule: Do not add @ts-ignore, @ts-expect-error, or any casts to any.; Do not change tsconfig.json or package.json.
rules: Do not add @ts-ignore, @ts-expect-error, or any casts to any.
Do not change tsconfig.json or package.json.

jobLines.text: Running npm run typecheck -- --strict must not report more errors in other files under src/ than it does now.
Keep every existing test passing, and keep the test count the same.

goal: Make `npm run typecheck -- --strict` report zero errors in src/checks.js while introducing no @ts-ignore, @ts-expect-error, or any-casts in that file and leaving tsconfig.json and package.json untouched, keep the strict-mode error count in other src/ files no higher than it is now, and keep every existing test passing with the same test count.

notes: Line 1's zero-error check and line 2's outside-src/checks.js ceiling: tsc invoked as `npx tsc --noEmit --strict` (the repo's own binary through npx, plus the --strict flag the person asked for). Line 2's population is src/ minus src/checks.js, read through scope.excludePrefixes on that one file.

The typecheck parser is the genre's tsc-error-line pattern with aggregate sum (capture null tallies one per error line), so a clean target scope legitimately reads a counted zero; line 1 additionally proves the command itself exited 0.

Test floor (line 3) counts EXECUTED tests via ^# tests (\d+)$ at seed baseline, so a skipped/deselected test cannot pad the count; suite-green proves both a clean exit and ^# fail 0. The 'reported test count (# pass / total) matches the seed' phrasing is covered as: executed total not below seed AND zero failures — I did not add a separate pass-count stage, since with zero failures pass==total.

no-suppressions (always-on) covers the confirmed check 'no @ts-ignore / @ts-expect-error / any casts added in the diff'; its 'any' pattern also flags legitimate uses of the word `any` in added lines of changed .js files, so a fix that legitimately needs `any` will fail that guard — that is the genre's fixed battery, not something I can loosen.
The confirmed check 'tsconfig.json and package.json are unchanged' is enforced by the always-on write fence (files-changed allowPrefixes [src/]) and is NOT composed again here, per the plan.

NOT CHECKED (the person asked for it but no stage measures it): a clean `npm run build:types` and the publish-time packed-tarball consumer install that type-checks published .d.ts files — outside the three numbered job lines.
The person's answer that other src/ files may change 'if needed, small' is not measurable as a magnitude; it is measured only as 'does not increase the error count outside src/checks.js' (line 2).
timeoutMs was left unset on every stage; I had no fact telling me typical typecheck/test durations for this repo.
